film.name: Clueless
film.description: Clueless (1995), directed by Amy Heckerling and starring Alicia Silverstone, Stacey Dash and Brittany Murphy, transposes Jane Austen’s Emma to a 1990s Beverly Hills high school as a teen comedy-romance. The film follows a privileged, style-obsessed student who plays matchmaker for friends and teachers, only to confront her own emotional shortcomings and grow up. Its sharp, pop-culture-savvy script, memorable performances and bold fashion aesthetic create a playful satire of wealth, identity and adolescent social climbing. The overall tone is witty, upbeat and warmly self-aware.

film.name: Groundhog Day
film.description: Groundhog Day (1993), directed by Harold Ramis and starring Bill Murray, Andie MacDowell and Chris Elliott, blends comedy, romance, fantasy and drama. Murray plays a cynical weatherman who becomes trapped reliving the same small‑town holiday repeatedly; over many iterations he moves from selfish cynicism to empathy, skillfulness and love. The film explores themes of redemption, personal growth and the search for meaning, balancing deadpan humor with heartfelt, philosophical reflection. Its warm, intimate visuals and montage‑driven repetition create a tone that is both funny and ultimately uplifting.

film.name: Notting Hill
film.description: Notting Hill (1999), directed by Roger Michell and written by Richard Curtis, is a romantic comedy-drama starring Hugh Grant and Julia Roberts. The story follows a London bookseller whose ordinary life collides with that of a world-famous actress, and their ensuing relationship is tested by paparazzi, public scrutiny and class differences. Grounded in a close-knit neighborhood and supported by a circle of friends, the film mixes warm humor with bittersweet emotional notes about fame, privacy and belonging.

film.name: Hidden Figures
film.description: Hidden Figures (2016), directed by Theodore Melfi and starring Taraji P. Henson, Octavia Spencer, and Janelle Monáe, is a biographical drama about three African-American mathematicians at NASA during the Space Race. The film dramatizes their vital mathematical work on early orbital missions and their struggles against racial and gender discrimination in a segregated workplace. Combining period detail with intimate character scenes, it emphasizes themes of perseverance, friendship, and the fight for recognition. The overall tone is uplifting and emotionally resonant, celebrating scientific achievement and social progress.

film.name: The Princess Bride
film.description: The Princess Bride (1987), directed by Rob Reiner and starring Cary Elwes, Mandy Patinkin, and Robin Wright, is a family-friendly blend of adventure, romance, and comedy. Framed as a grandfather reading a tale to his grandson, it follows a farmhand who becomes a pirate and undertakes a quest filled with swordfights, giants, and cunning villains to reunite with his true love. The film balances swashbuckling set pieces and fairy-tale romance with witty, self-aware humor and enduring quotable dialogue, exploring themes of love, revenge, friendship, and the redemptive power of stories.

film.name: The Wedding Planner
film.description: The Wedding Planner (2001), directed by Adam Shankman and starring Jennifer Lopez and Matthew McConaughey, is a glossy romantic comedy about a consummate wedding planner whose professional world is upended when she falls for the groom of a major client. Set in San Francisco and featuring a wealthy-client subplot and familial expectations, the film mixes light humor with emotional beats as characters confront duty versus desire. Thematically it explores professional ethics, family pressure, and the search for an authentic relationship, all conveyed in a warm, feel-good tone.

memo.audience: The audience skews heavily female (+0.53 female, -0.53 male) and concentrates among younger adults, over-indexing at ages 25 to 29 (+0.230) and 24 and younger (+0.132). It under-indexes across older brackets: 30 to 34 (-0.223), 35 to 44 (-0.407), 45 to 54 (-0.126), and 55 and older (-0.162). Core thematic interests include 'british', 'British Literature', 'Culture Clash', 'Ensemble Cast', 'choral', and 'classical'.
memo.marketing: Sponsorship and co-marketing opportunities include fashion and luxury brands Calvin Klein (affinity 0.9368, lift 0.4370), Tommy Hilfiger (affinity 0.9365, lift 0.4370), Ray-ban (affinity 0.9331, lift 0.4348), and Burberry (affinity 0.9303, lift 0.4306). Targeted promotional audio channels include podcasts 'Life Will Be the Death of Me with Chelsea Handler' (affinity 0.8887, lift 0.4454), 'I Weigh with Jameela Jamil' (affinity 0.8861, lift 0.4271), 'Getting Curious with Jonathan Van Ness' (affinity 0.9194, lift 0.4229), and 'Armchair Expert with Dax Shepard' (affinity 0.9187, lift 0.4190). TV affinities feature shows like 'Can't Cope, Won't Cope' (affinity 0.9514, lift 0.9514) and 'Sensitive Skin' (affinity 0.9536, lift 0.8035).
memo.recommendation: We recommend greenlighting a stage musical adaptation of Notting Hill. It outperforms all other titles tested, scoring in the 97th percentile of musical-theatre fan affinity and qualifying for the Strong fit tier where over half of historical adaptations ran 500+ performances. Its blend of high-profile romance, British charm, and ensemble comedy aligns directly with the core theatrical demographic.

reasons.evidence: Notting Hill recorded an affinity score of 0.8619 (97th percentile), topping Clueless (0.8576, 93rd percentile), Hidden Figures (0.8425, 88th percentile), The Wedding Planner (0.8417, 88th percentile), Sister Act 2: Back in the Habit (0.8067, 60th percentile), The Princess Bride (0.7985, 48th percentile), Ghost (0.7960, 45th percentile), and Groundhog Day (0.7477, 24th percentile). Ambiguities were resolved to the 1990 Ghost and 1993 Sister Act 2.
reasons.claim: Notting Hill achieves the highest audience fit score among all eight candidates evaluated.
The film falls into the Strong fit band, historically associated with long Broadway runs.
reasons.evidence: Films in the Strong fit band have a historical median run of 565 performances, with 52.6% achieving 500+ performances. Comparables include Once (1,167 performances), Legally Blonde (595 performances), and Meet Me in St. Louis (252 performances).

Audience profiling indicates shared descriptors with musical-theatre fans including 'Drama', 'Comedy', 'Romance', 'Heartwarming', 'Romantic', 'Charming', 'Endearing', 'Star-Crossed Lovers', 'Celebrity', and 'Romantic Comedy'.
reasons.claim: Shared appeal with musical-theatre audiences centers on classic romantic comedy dynamics.

nextSteps: Approach rights-holders to explore theatrical adaptation rights for Notting Hill.
Initiate creative outreach to compatible songwriting teams and composers such as Elton John.
Begin development of a stage book accentuating the film's ensemble cast and culture-clash romance.
Explore early brand partnerships with apparel partners such as Burberry and Tommy Hilfiger.
memo.tour: Key touring markets showing top index include Tulsa, OK (score: 0.9997, 3 cells), Philadelphia, PA (score: 0.9980, 1 cell), Nashville, TN (score: 0.9970, 3 cells), and Birmingham, AL (score: 0.9954, 1 cell).
risks: Affinity scores measure audience fit and interest, not a guaranteed commercial outcome; book quality, score, staging, casting, capitalization, and timing remain decisive.
Strong fit comparables exhibit performance variability, spanning from 252 performances (Meet Me in St. Louis) to 1,167 performances (Once).
The audience under-indexes among patrons aged 35 to 54 and 55+, demographics that are foundational to traditional Broadway subscriptions and group ticket sales.
memo.creative: Ideal creative and talent considerations include composers such as Elton John (affinity 0.9222, lift 0.4224), Michael Bublé (affinity 0.9388, lift 0.4391), Adele (affinity 0.9355, lift 0.4357), or John Mayer (affinity 0.9209, lift 0.4210). For prospective cast, high-affinity names include Michelle Dockery (affinity 0.8964, lift 0.4817), Rachel Brosnahan (affinity 0.8990, lift 0.4641), Joshua Jackson (affinity 0.8976, lift 0.4927), and Chris Noth (affinity 0.8993, lift 0.4899).
memo.headline: Notting Hill leads all eight evaluated properties in musical-theatre audience affinity, placing in the 97th percentile and Strong fit category.
